When a block is placed in an open pan full of water:
If : The block floats or stays submerged by displacing its own weight of water. Since the pan is open and full, the displaced water overflows. The total weight on that side of the pan remains unchanged, and equilibrium is maintained.

However, because the block is denser than water, the weight of the block is greater than the weight of the displaced water. This creates an extra downward force on one side, destroying the equilibrium. Therefore, equilibrium is only maintained if the block does not add more weight than the water it displaces.

Explain Question:
Analyzing the shift in the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution of kinetic energies when temperature increases.

Concept:
Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution and temperature.

Solution:
The Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution curve shows how many molecules in a sample prowess a certain amount of kinetic energy. 1 when the temperature (T) is increased, the following changes occur:
(1) Shift to the right: the most probable kinetic energy increases because the molecules move faster on average. The peak of the graph moves toward higher energy values.
(2)Flattening on the peak: since the total number of molecules (the area under the curve) must remain constant, the peak must become lower as the curve spreads out over a wider range of energies.
(3)Area I vs. Area II:
        Area I (Low-energy region): As the curve flattens and shift right, the proportion of molecules with lower kinetic energy decreases.
        Area II (High-energy region) The ‘’ tail’’ of the curve on the right side becomes higher, representing an increase in the fraction of molecules with high kinetic energy (specifically those exceeding the activation                energy).  

Final Answer: option (4)
